details: Production's Victorian branch predates the standard identifiers and has a UUID, so a policy address derived from the branch ID would be unusable and the import could not target the existing branch without creating a duplicate. - branch records may carry an explicit public slug (vic, nat); - the registry resolves /policies/<slug>/ and import targets by that slug; - ratification writes the branch slug onto new policy records; - the standard branch migration backfills a missing slug without renaming, re-parenting or un-recognising an existing branch; - the import CLI accepts either the branch ID or its public slug.

summary: Branch policy registry import, branch-scoped URLs and post-ratification policy changes (#90)
details: * feat(policies): import adopted branch policy with explicit provenance (#89) A branch may already hold policy adopted outside Engage. The import treats that as a provenance operation, not a proposal flow: - reads a branch policy feed and validates every record before writing; - requires an explicit authority basis and fails closed without one; - writes a published, adopted registry record plus an immutable policy_revision holding the exact source document and content hash; - records the source, authority basis, timestamps and provenance lineage; - reports created, unchanged, changed, conflicting, invalid and missing records without overwriting anything; - never republishes a record that was withdrawn, superseded or repealed. Dry-run and re-run are safe: only 'create' entries write, every write is keyed, and a changed source is a review item for the change lifecycle rather than a silent rewrite. * feat(policies): branch-scoped registry and changes to adopted policy (#89, #37) The registry is now navigable by authority and topic, and adopted policy can change through a proposal instead of being frozen at publication. Registry: - policy addresses become /policies/<branch>/<slug>/; internal IDs stay stable and legacy /policies/<id>/ addresses redirect to the canonical path; - the registry collates by adopting branch, then by the branch's own topics, so 41 Victorian policies are browsable rather than one flat list; - each branch has its own registry page with adoption basis, source and current/past tabs; a search and branch filter remain available; - rows show title, two-line summary, topic, branch and adoption origin; - imported records show their authority, import date and source. Post-ratification lifecycle: - a proposal may declare targetPolicyId and amend/replace/repeal; the target is fixed at creation against the exact published revision; - the policy page shows the proposed changes separately and never implies a draft has changed adopted policy; - ratification of a repeal records the deciding proposal; an amendment or replacement supersedes the predecessor only when the successor is published, so the public registry never shows a gap; - imported and Engage-ratified lineage read together in the same history. * chore(changelog): refresh public changelog for policy registry work * fix(policies): clear search and branch filters together in the registry * chore(changelog): include registry filter fix in the snapshot * chore(changelog): refresh snapshot at merge head * fix(policies): use the ballot-scoped result filter in policy detail

summary: Cover governance writes on a MongoDB replica set (#91)
details: * test(governance): cover governance writes on a MongoDB replica set Add replica-set cases for the deletion guard, stage-transition audit events, formal-decision idempotency and conditional-write concurrency. The in-memory database cannot prove transactions, unique indexes or race behaviour, so each case is skipped without VOTING_TEST_MONGODB_URI and drops its own database. Covers known gap 17 (docs/status/known-gaps.md) and RFC 0001 cross-slice risk 4. * test(governance): adapt replica-set coverage to closed-ballot certification #28 requires a closed ballot before a result can be recorded, and checks the recorded result against the votes bound to the ballot and revision. Close the fixtures as the scheduler does and record the zero-vote certifications as explicit overrides, so the atomicity, idempotency and concurrency cases keep testing what they claim. Adds a real-MongoDB case proving an open ballot cannot be certified, that the refusal writes no result, and that certification succeeds after closure with the computed tally stored.

summary: Validate recorded outcomes against the bound tally (#28) (#86)
details: * feat(ballots): validate recorded outcomes against the bound tally Record a formal ballot outcome only after comparing the officer's result with the outcome computed from the votes bound to that ballot and immutable revision (#28). The comparison is deliberately limited to what the decision register settles: Yes greater than No approves and a tie does not (D9); abstentions are recorded and excluded rather than given a denominator (D10, O1); no quorum, turnout or minimum-participation threshold applies (D8). The basis is versioned as `simple-majority-d9-v1`. A contradicting result is refused unless the officer supplies a written reason, and is then stored as an explicit override. The result keeps the tally at certification, the rule basis and the computed result; the `decision.recorded` event records the actor, reason, computed result and recorded result alongside the existing atomic result and ballot certification. Identical retries remain idempotent, conflicting replacements are refused, and historical results are returned unchanged and never rewritten. Both admin result forms now show the computed outcome and its tally before submission and require the override reason when the chosen result contradicts it, using the shared Field, Textarea and Badge primitives. * test(ballots): cover computed outcomes, overrides and stored evidence Add rule-level cases for approval, rejection, a tie, zero votes and abstention-heavy ballots, plus the two admin form behaviours that reveal and require an override reason. Add real-MongoDB replica-set coverage for the parts that prove persistence and the ordered result write: the tally and rule basis stored on the result, rejection of a contradiction without a reason, an audited override, idempotent retries, refused replacement, encrypted-ballot certification through the decryption path, and a historical result that stays readable and unrewritten. The result API is exercised end to end with the dev session. Refs #28. * docs(governance): record computed ballot outcome validation Describe the computed Yes-versus-No check, its `simple-majority-d9-v1` basis, the stored tally and the audited override in the lifecycle, API and agent guides. Mark known gap 10 as partly resolved and keep #28/L1 Partial because the abstention denominator (O1), quorum and ranked choice remain undecided. * chore(changelog): regenerate the public changelog snapshot * feat(ballots): certify only a closed ballot from a consistent bound tally Refuse certification while a ballot can still accept votes. A result is accepted when the ballot has a closure marker, its close time has passed, or the system has already closed it; a live ballot returns BALLOT_NOT_CLOSED and a ballot with no recorded close is refused rather than assumed closed, because a later vote could contradict an early certification. Tally only votes bound to the ballot and exact revision, and treat the rest as a ballot defect instead of ignoring them: unbound or mismatched-revision votes now return BALLOT_TALLY_UNBOUND_VOTES, unreadable encrypted votes return BALLOT_TALLY_UNREADABLE, and missing or invalid decryption keys return BALLOT_DECRYPTION_UNAVAILABLE (503). The tally query reads only the fields the check needs. Reject an override reason longer than 1000 characters instead of truncating audit evidence, and treat a retry that changes the recorded override reason as a conflict rather than an idempotent success. The refusal message now names the computed outcome and says that any other result, including inconclusive, requires a written reason. Refs #28. * feat(admin): show the enforced tally and recorded outcomes Derive the admin outcome basis from the same bound tally that certification enforces, so a page can no longer show a tally the server will not count. A zero-vote ballot reads "No votes yet — outcome not yet computable" instead of "Unsuccessful", and an unbound or unreadable tally is named instead of guessed. An open ballot shows when voting closes instead of an unusable result form; once a result exists both admin surfaces render the recorded outcome, computed result, tally and override reason instead of a re-submittable form. Revealing the override field moves focus to it and announces the requirement to assistive technology. Show overridden outcomes in Ballots & decisions with the reason available, and add the computed result, rule basis and override to the proposal PDF report. Refs #28. * test(ballots): cover closure, the bound set and override integrity Close fixtures exactly as the scheduler does before certifying, and pin the override rule in the two pre-existing suites by asserting the refusal when the reason is removed rather than only supplying one. Add replica-set cases for a live ballot that cannot be certified and the changed closed tally that is then certified, a vote on another revision or with no revision, amendment-ballot votes excluded from the matter tally, an unreadable encrypted vote, missing decryption keys, an over-length override reason and a retry that rewrites the recorded reason. Cover the form focus/announcement behaviour and the PDF computed/override rows. Refs #28. * docs(legal): correct the terms to describe computed ballot outcomes Terms of Use §9 claimed Engage "does not calculate or apply a passing threshold", which is no longer true. Describe the versioned simple-majority-d9-v1 rule, the tie and zero-vote result, the treatment of abstentions, the absence of quorum or turnout, and the explicit, reasoned and audited override. The acceptance gate stays inactive: the document remains owner-authorised with no effective date. The incorrect sentence was in the Terms of Use, not the Privacy Policy, so the Privacy Policy and its version are unchanged. Roll the Terms to version 1.1 and record the correction and the #40 follow-up in the privacy review. Refs #28, #40. * docs(governance): record closed-ballot certification and the bound tally Document that certification requires a closed ballot, that unbound votes and unreadable votes are refused, that inconclusive is always an explicit override, and that amendment endorsement ballots remain officer-supplied because O2/D18 are undecided. Correct the failure table so a zero-vote unsuccessful result needs no override, refresh the tracker, known gaps and handover status, and point the agent guide at the corrected Terms section. Refs #28. * chore(changelog): regenerate the public changelog snapshot * test(ballots): warm the route database before asserting on it The result-API case resolved the application client only inside the route. A transient connect failure could make the development fallback serve the in-memory database, so the route could not see the fixture and the test failed with a confusing authorisation-style error. Resolve the application client in the test and assert the fixture is visible before exercising the route, so a real connectivity failure fails loudly instead of degrading silently. Refs #28. * chore(changelog): record the review fixes in the public snapshot * fix(ballots): judge each ballot's own close time and keep zero-vote outcomes computable Read the addressed ballot's row before the matter so a second, still-open ballot on a closed matter is refused instead of inheriting the matter's closure. The matter fields remain the fallback for legacy ballots with no ballot row. Return the computed outcome for every computable tally, including a zero-vote ballot (still "unsuccessful" under D9), so the UI can require an override instead of silently withholding the reason field. Separate a missing key ring from unreadable votes: the display summary now reports `decryption-unavailable` on its own, with unbound votes stated first because that is the cause an officer can act on. Add a tolerant key loader for read-only paths so a broken key ring no longer fails a page that renders no encrypted votes; signed-in list and detail reads use it, while casting and certification stay strict. The result route now reports a clean BALLOT_DECRYPTION_UNAVAILABLE (503) instead of leaking key-configuration detail. Refs #28. * fix(admin): keep the visible result status and render every tally state The hidden override announcement was the first `[role="status"]` in the result form, so `querySelector('[role="status"]')` returned it and every success or refusal was written to an invisible node. The announcement now uses `aria-live="polite"` without `role="status"`, and both submit handlers target the visible line through `formStatusRegion`, so feedback remains sighted-visible and still announced. Show the computed outcome for a zero-vote ballot instead of claiming it is not computable, which also restores the override field for `Successful` and `Inconclusive`. Add explicit states for unavailable decryption keys and separate unreadable votes, and withhold the form while the tally is defective rather than offering an action the server will refuse. Refs #28. * test(ballots): cover per-ballot closure, zero-vote overrides and the status line Prove an open second ballot on a closed matter is refused while its closed sibling certifies, and that a zero-vote ballot records successful only with a written reason. Pin the tally-state precedence (unbound before unreadable), distinguish missing keys from unreadable votes, and assert display key loading degrades to null instead of throwing. Guard the UI regression: the announcement is not a `[role="status"]`, both pages use `formStatusRegion`, and that helper returns the visible line when the hidden node comes first in the form. Refs #28. * docs(governance): correct the legal pointer and merge wording The privacy review said the Privacy Policy describes the computed rule; the Privacy Policy is deliberately unchanged and the correction is in the Terms of Use. Correct that sentence, rename the lifecycle row so it describes the zero-vote case rather than implying every untallied result needs an override, qualify the display-versus-enforcement claim, and state per-ballot closure. Align the tracker and handover on "integrated, branch only; not merged". Refs #28, #40. * chore(changelog): record the second-pass review fixes * chore(changelog): include the final verification commits * fix(ballots): let display reads degrade instead of failing on unreadable votes Add an opt-in `tolerateUnreadableVotes` read mode to `listProposals` and `getProposalDetail`. Admin pages use it so a broken key ring renders an explicit "decryption unavailable" state instead of returning 500, and affected rows carry `unreadableVoteCount` so the missing votes are counted and shown rather than quietly dropped. Every other read keeps today's loud failure, and certification is untouched. Refs #28. * fix(ballots): key results by ballot, share closure state and reject stray override reasons Add `proposalBallotResultFilter` so the result attached to a matter's primary ballot is addressed by `ballotId` (legacy results without a ballotId still resolve). Apply it to the admin workspace, the proposal PDF, the public proposal and policy pages and the matter read model, so a result on one ballot no longer shadows another. Add `resolveBallotClosure` as the single closure rule used by the server gate and the pages: the addressed ballot's own status/close time first, the matter as the fallback. Add `ballotOutcomeLabel` for consistent title-case rendering and fix the quadratic vote grouping in `readBoundBallotTallies`. Refuse a written `overrideReason` when the result already matches the computed outcome (`RESULT_OVERRIDE_REASON_UNEXPECTED`, 400) instead of accepting it once and then failing an identical retry, so a reason is never silently discarded. Refs #28. * fix(admin): derive the result and closure state from the balloted record Use the shared closure rule on both canvassing surfaces and the oversight page so the form is offered exactly when certification would accept it, including the case where a sibling ballot's close time differs from the matter's. Look up recorded results by the primary ballot, show "N unreadable" when the display tally is partial, and render computed outcomes in title case alongside recorded results. Refs #28. * test(ballots): cover closure precedence, per-ballot results and stray reasons Add pure cases for closure precedence (ballot row before matter) and outcome labels, and replica-set cases proving an unnecessary override reason is refused rather than silently dropped, that display reads tolerate unreadable votes while strict reads still fail, and that primary and sibling results resolve to their own ballots. Refs #28. * docs(legal): scope the outcome rule to ordinary Yes/No ballots Say that the computed simple-majority rule applies to ordinary Yes/No ballots on a matter, and that amendment endorsement ballots follow a separate procedure recorded by an authorised officer. The publication status and the inactive acceptance gate are unchanged; this stays inside the existing unreleased Terms version 1.1. Refs #28, #40. * docs(governance): record stray-reason refusal and display degradation Document that a reason supplied for a matching result is refused rather than dropped, that a broken key ring degrades admin displays to an explicit unavailable state with unreadable votes counted while certification stays strict, and keep the Terms-of-Use pointer and per-ballot closure precedence accurate. Refs #28. * chore(changelog): record the merge and third-pass fixes

summary: Make the ballot_results index migration preflighted and recoverable (#55) (#83)
details: * feat(ballots): make the ballot_results index migration explicit and recoverable Startup no longer creates or drops the ballot_results indexes as a silent side effect. A legacy collection is reported and left untouched; a fresh one still receives the indexes; an already-migrated one is a no-op. `npm run ballots:results-index` adds preflight, dry-run, apply, verify and recovery commands. Apply backs up the index definitions and documents before change, proves the unique partial ballotId index before dropping the legacy unique proposalId index, verifies the final state, and records the actor and backup in data_migrations. Failures are recorded and re-raised instead of being swallowed. Duplicate results are reported for human reconciliation; nothing deletes or rewrites ballot results to make an index fit. Tests: eight replica-set cases cover a fresh install, legacy startup, duplicate blockers, dry run, full apply, partial apply, re-run, loud failure and recovery reporting. The Sprint 1 integrity test now asserts the explicit contract rather than the old startup upgrade. Also records PR #51 as merged to main and the resolved migration risk (#55). Closes #55 * chore(changelog): record the ballot-results index migration * docs(security): record Turnstile as merged to main

summary: RFC 0001: Sprint 1 integration, Phase 1 lifecycle, rendering performance and Turnstile (#51)
details: * docs(rfc): propose platform evolution and integrity programme * fix(governance): enforce ballot deadlines, rebinding, atomic decisions, and deletion guards (#26, #50) * fix(membership): guard CRM-sourced memberships, exempt national row from conflict, and record manual provenance (#32) * fix(rbac): consolidate permission enforcement, ballot binding gate, and ratification authority checks (#27, #31) * fix(proposals): clear provenance without a conflicting stage update Staff editing a proposal through the admin form always submits provenance: null for the default 'clear provenance' option. saveProposal placed provenance in both $set and $unset, which MongoDB rejects with a path conflict, so every staff edit failed against a real database. Make the clear and set branches mutually exclusive and cover the case against the real MongoDB voting suite. * fix(ballots): keep the deadline banner hydration-stable The ballot deadline rendered a server date and a post-mount relative time in the same text nodes. React 19 reported a text hydration mismatch on every ballot with a deadline, forcing an unnecessary client re-render. Mark the two intentionally time-dependent nodes as hydration-stable and make the date helper's timezone explicit so server and client markup match before the viewer-local deadline replaces it. * test(rbac): reconcile Sprint 1 authority expectations after integration The governance branch made ballots.bind and a future closing date mandatory when entering Decide, and refuses deletion of matters with governance history. The RBAC branch assumed neither. Align the fixtures with real session permissions, supply a ballot deadline, and delete a draft with no history. Ignore branch grants for permissions the catalogue reserves to National scope, allow branch-scoped comment moderation, and prove that a branch proposals.delete grant does not confer destructive authority. * docs(rfc): integrate Sprint 1 and record maintainer decisions Add the canonical governance decision register, the RFC 0001 programme tracker and the Sprint 1 integration report. Update the documentation index and replace the open-question list with the decisions now supplied, while keeping genuinely unresolved questions explicit. Add a browser verification script for the deadline, voting and vote-change journeys and record its evidence. * chore(changelog): refresh snapshot for the Sprint 1 integration * docs(rfc): track active workstreams and new implementation issues Record the Phase 1, rendering-performance and Turnstile workstreams, link the new issues for performance (#52), the command layer (#53), the decision record and responsibility queue (#54), and ballot-results migration safety (#55). Clarify that #36 is deferred rather than blocked inside this programme. * docs(rfc): correct membership workstream status The CRM branch did not add the unique branch-membership index or the duplicate-resolving migration required by #32, so I3 remains partial. * feat(lifecycle): second proposals and schedule advancement and ballot closure Implements the approved lifecycle schedule from the decision register (D3-D7, RFC 0001 Phase 1, refs #26 and #30). - A verified member who is not the author may second a proposal while it is in Propose. The act records `secondedBy`, `secondedAt` and `deliberationEndsAt` (30 days) and writes `proposal.seconded`. It does not change the stage or grant ballot authority. - `src/lib/lifecycle-schedule.ts` is the single source of truth for the 30-day deliberation period, 30-day ballot period and 60-day ceiling. - A system actor (`system:lifecycle-scheduler`) advances due deliberations to Decide, binding the latest immutable revision and setting `ballotClosesAt = secondedAt + 60 days`. It requires no `ballots.bind`; the human early-advancement gate is unchanged. - Advancement fails closed on unresolved amendments (`rejected`, `withdrawn`, `applied`, `not-endorsed` and `inconclusive` are the only non-blocking statuses), on votes bound to other wording, on a missing seconding anchor, and on a ceiling already in the past. - Ballots close automatically at their deadline: `ballot.closed` is recorded once, the stage and result are untouched, and voting is refused after the boundary (D12 is not implemented). - Conditional filters, deterministic event IDs and transactional writes make both operations idempotent and safe under concurrent runs. - An officer opening a ballot without a date now receives the 30-day default; explicit dates remain authoritative. - Adds a read-only report for legacy ballots without deadlines and matters in Deliberate without a deliberation clock. * feat(ops): add governance scheduler and deadline migration report commands - `npm run governance:scheduler` runs the lifecycle scheduler as a dry run by default and writes only with `--apply`. It prints a JSON report with advanced, skipped, closed, blockers and errors, and exits non-zero on errors. - `npm run governance:migration-report` prints the read-only legacy report. - Both require MONGODB_URI and fail loudly without it; neither adds a daemon nor requires production credentials. * docs(lifecycle): document seconding, scheduled transitions and closure Records the implemented behaviour and the assumptions visible for review: - one seconder who is not the author; seconding records the clock but does not change the stage or gate Propose -> Deliberate; - automatic proposal advancement at the deliberation deadline by a system actor, without `ballots.bind`; - the conservative blocking-amendment set, reason codes and failure behaviour; - automatic closure at the ballot deadline without a stage change or result; - the 30-day default for officer-opened ballots; - new proposal fields (`secondedBy`, `secondedAt`, `deliberationEndsAt`, `ballotClosedAt`), deterministic event IDs and scheduler transaction rules; - the read-only migration report and its manual recovery options. * chore(changelog): refresh snapshot for the Phase 1 lifecycle work * docs(lifecycle): state that returning to Propose keeps the seconding clock * chore(changelog): include the lifecycle documentation commits * feat(security): verify Turnstile tokens for unauthenticated actions Add server-side Cloudflare Turnstile verification (D32) and a shared MongoDB fixed-window limiter for the abuse-prone unauthenticated routes. - protect Sense Box submission, magic-link sign-in/first registration, and email sign-up if it is enabled later - fail closed with 503 and an operational error when production requires Turnstile but the secret or site key is missing - report missing, invalid, expired, replayed and malformed tokens with plain-language errors; never log or return the secret or token - store only a keyed hash of the client address, with a TTL index, so limits are shared across instances - leave authenticated voting, deliberation and admin writes untouched - tests cover configuration states, verification outcomes, route refusal and acceptance, real-MongoDB concurrency and the voting exemption * feat(security): show the Turnstile widget on protected forms Render Cloudflare Turnstile on the Sense Box and magic-link sign-in forms using Horizon primitives. The widget renders nothing when no site key is configured, reports load and expiry failures inline with a retry action, and asks for a fresh token after a rejected submission because tokens are single-use. * docs(security): document Turnstile enforcement and rate limits Record the protected actions, configuration contract, fail-closed states, failure messages, privacy boundary, rate-limit defaults and remaining gaps (CSP and headers stay with #38). Add the new keys to the environment example. * chore(changelog): refresh snapshot for Turnstile abuse protection * docs(security): name the rate-limit collection plainly * perf(tooling): add rendering performance harness and DB command metrics Adds an opt-in MongoDB command monitor (disabled unless ENGAGE_DB_COMMAND_MONITOR=1 and APP_MODE is not production), a development-only diagnostics route, and a repeatable Playwright/Mongo measurement harness with baseline and comparison modes. No production behaviour changes. * perf(proposals): batch independent detail reads and defer ballot hydration Runs supersede, eligibility, related-branch and evidence reads with the rest of the proposal-detail batch instead of in sequence. The ballot hydrates on idle rather than blocking load; the stance selector does the same. * perf(auth): resolve a session once per request render Layouts and pages each asked for the same session. Cache the in-flight resolution against the Request object so one browser request performs one session lookup while role revocation remains request-scoped. Adds a regression test for reuse. * perf(lists): project list reads and reuse member vote queries Stops list queries returning detailHtml and, where no search depends on it, long rationale text. Home and the proposals list reuse one member-vote read for outstanding ballots; the member page loads shared activity inputs once instead of twice. Member-page islands in inactive views hydrate only when visible. Adds visibility and vote-reuse regression tests. * perf(admin): consolidate register reads and defer participation panel The proposals register now reads the proposal collection once and batches amendment and revision lookups instead of issuing one query per row. The overview's recent-participation panel moves to a server island with a stable fallback, so its session-dependent reads no longer block the dashboard. Admin timelines hydrate when visible; migrations hydrate on idle. * perf(client): defer notification hydration off the critical path The header notification bell and notification preferences hydrate when the browser is idle. The bell is secondary to page content but still loads its unread count; no API or preference behaviour changes. * docs(status): record the rendering performance audit and measurements Classifies initial, deferred and interaction-only data per audited page; records baseline and after medians, queries removed or deferred, bundle findings, limitations and the highest-value remaining work. Adds a pnpm/npm perf:render entry point. * chore(changelog): refresh snapshot for the rendering performance slice * fix(admin): render saved values in select controls Astro renders React component slot children as raw HTML, so React never sees the options inside NativeSelect and cannot apply defaultValue. Every select rendered its first option, which meant editing a proposal could silently reset its stage, clearing provenance, changing a member's status to pending, or applying the wrong filter or sort. Mark the stored option as selected at each affected call site. The admin proposal editor and register, member administration, Sense Box review, engagement period, policy filters and public proposal filters are covered. * feat(proposals): make seconding the act that opens deliberation D3 requires a seconder before Deliberate and D4 anchors the clock to seconding. The initial Phase 1 implementation recorded the seconding but left Propose -> Deliberate to an officer, which could stall a proposal indefinitely and run the clock in the wrong stage. Seconding now performs the transition and records both the seconding and the stage transition. Officer and API transitions into Deliberate are refused without a recorded seconder. A member-facing control appears on the proposal page for eligible, non-author members, with inline feedback and no raw controls. details: Add notification_outbox, written immediately after a committed lifecycle transition and drained by npm run notifications:drain (dry-run by default, --apply to send). Two events are wired: a ballot opened by the lifecycle scheduler (new_ballots) and an open ballot inside the approved seven-day window (closing_deadlines). The audience is the voting electorate. Candidates are confirmed with getProposalEligibility and canViewProposal, the same predicate and visibility gate used when casting a vote, and eligibility is checked again at drain time so a revoked membership is suppressed rather than notified. Rows carry one unique dedupeKey per member, ballot and event; the drain claims with a conditional lease, retries at 1/2/4/8 minutes and stops at five attempts. Terminal rows carry a two-year retention TTL. Enqueue and delivery can never fail, block or alter a governance transition, and the scheduler report is unchanged. governance_outcomes and contribution_responses stay unwired: the result route is being refactored and the comment-outcome event needs a product decision.

summary: Response headers, hash-based CSP and cross-origin enforcement (#38) (#100)
details: * feat(security): add perimeter headers, CSP and cross-site request rule Every response now carries nosniff, a strict referrer policy, frame denial, a minimal Permissions-Policy and a Content Security Policy. HSTS is sent only in production when HTTPS is provable. The policy keeps Astro's build-time script and style hashes and allows only the external hosts the app uses: Cloudflare Turnstile (script, frame, connect) and the first-party Plausible host (script, connect). Inline style attributes are allowed through style-src-attr only, because tally and progress bars use them; script-src has no unsafe-inline and no directive permits unsafe-eval. The service-worker registration was is:inline, which Astro does not hash, so it is now a processed script. Astro's form-post origin check is kept, and allowedDomains trusts the production host over HTTPS so its comparison uses the public origin behind the proxy. The middleware adds what Astro's check deliberately exempts: every state-changing method, JSON bodies, a cross-site Sec-Fetch-Site, an Origin that differs from the trusted public origin, and an absent Origin when a session or dev cookie is present. Bearer cron calls and webhooks carry no cookie and stay allowed. Refs #38 * test(security): verify the CSP and origin rule in a real browser The production build is served with a disposable in-memory database. Chromium checks the home, proposal, sign-in and Sense Box pages for CSP violations, console errors and failed requests; proves the Turnstile script and frame and the Plausible script and event endpoint reach the network layer; asserts the document and JSON header sets; and shows same-origin fetches and native form posts succeed while browser, JSON and cookie-without-Origin state-changing requests are refused. Cloudflare and Plausible are intercepted and answered locally; the script never contacts production. Refs #38 * docs(security): record the perimeter header set, CSP and origin rule Adds docs/security/perimeter.md as the operating contract for headers, CSP sources and the cross-site rule, with the exact values, every external host and its reason, the scoped style-src-attr allowance, verification commands and residual risk. Corrects the pages that said there is no middleware and that a CSP, HSTS, frame or content-type headers are absent, updates the Turnstile and API/authorisation contracts, and records the #38 and I10 state in the programme tracker and known gaps. Remaining work is explicit: proxy headers for static assets and Astro's early 403, a reporting endpoint, CSRF tokens, and production header observation. Refs #38 * chore(changelog): refresh snapshot for the perimeter security slice Refs #38 * docs(security): clarify origin-check exemptions and deployment requirements States the form-like and safe-method exemptions precisely, scopes includeSubDomains to the sending host rather than fusionparty.org.au, and records that production must configure PUBLIC_ORIGIN or BETTER_AUTH_URL or browser writes are refused against the proxy's localhost origin. Refs #38

summary: Durable job records and operational health checks (#39) (#99)
details: * feat(ops): record authorised scheduled runs in a durable job ledger Add a job_runs collection with a 90-day TTL on startedAt and a withJobRun helper that records success or failure after the job finishes. A failed ledger write or summariser is logged and never changes the job result or error, so observability cannot break the thing it observes. Wire the governance scheduler (apply and dry-run), the ballot digest endpoint and the membership verification endpoint. Only authorised runs are recorded: 401 and 409 responses are not scheduled runs. Status codes, bodies, secrets, scheduling and governance writes are unchanged. Refs #39 * feat(ops): add exit-coded operational health checks and ops:health Evaluate governance scheduler recency and errors, ballot deadlines that passed without closure, digest cadence and held deliveries, verification recency and due backlog, recent failed or held email, and Turnstile configuration. Every threshold is named in the report and settable by environment variable; checks are count-only and never expose secrets, provider responses, member identifiers or ballot choices. /api/health now publishes coarse governanceScheduler and jobs states. A database failure stays 503, while a degraded job stays 200 so a container restart loop cannot hide a missing external scheduler. npm run ops:health prints JSON (or --human) and exits 0 healthy, 2 degraded or unknown, 1 failing or unreachable, requiring MONGODB_URI. Refs #39 * docs(ops): record job cadence, health command and runbook Document the job_runs ledger, the documented cadence and stale thresholds for each scheduled job, the ops:health command and exit codes, what each degraded state means, the maintainer escalation placeholder and the runbook actions. Record explicitly that production cron wiring and production verification are not done, so #39 remains partial. Update the tracker I10/S8 rows and known gap 21. Refs #39 * chore(changelog): refresh snapshot for the operational observability slice Refs #39 * fix(ops): warn before a scheduled job reaches its fail threshold A 15-minute job judged healthy for 24 hours leaves a full day blind to a complete outage. Each time-based check now has two tiers: degraded past warn (governance scheduler 2h, digest 1h, verification 2h) and failing past fail (26h, 24h, 24h). Within warn stays ok; a missing run stays failing; a failed last run stays failing. Warn and fail are configurable with the existing fail variables plus GOVERNANCE_SCHEDULER_WARN_HOURS, DIGEST_WARN_HOURS and MEMBERSHIP_VERIFICATION_WARN_HOURS. A warn value that is not below fail reports unknown with the conflicting values instead of trusting either. The report's thresholds block names both values and their source. Check ids, report shape, the ledger and route behaviour are unchanged; ops:health still exits 2 degraded and 1 failing. Refs #39 * docs(ops): document two-tier warn and fail job thresholds Show cadence, warn and fail for each scheduled job, explain that warn is a small multiple of cadence (not one missed tick) and why a 24-hour-only alert hid 96 missed 15-minute ticks, and record the invalid-pair behaviour, per-state meanings and escalation timing. Refs #39 * chore(changelog): refresh snapshot for the two-tier thresholds Refs #39 * fix(ops): report a failing job as failing on the health probe * chore(changelog): refresh after rewriting the synthetic token fixture
